title: The Ticket Confirms What the Marshal Already Called, Explained
subtitle: Ronja Oyelaran, Fenna Okoro and Casimir Beng on what a numbered ticket settles at a taxi rank, and where the other arguments go
summary: A research explainer from the School of Emergent Priorities on Ronja Oyelaran, Fenna Okoro and Casimir Beng's taxonomy of queue-order disputes at airport taxi ranks. It follows the argument over whose turn it is from ranks run on a marshal's call to ranks with a numbered-ticket dispenser, and shows where the disputes the ticket doesn't settle go. Oyelaran, Okoro and Beng describe the work in their own words.
topic: A research explainer of the paper coding a seven-category taxonomy of queue-order disputes across airport taxi ranks with and without a numbered-ticket dispenser, which finds the dispenser all but ends arrival-order disputes while total disputes hold steady and move to break re-entry

beats.text: Mostly to drivers coming back from a break
A numbered-ticket dispenser resolves the dispute it names and leaves the rest of the rank’s boarding-order contestation to relocate.
We expected the dispenser to close the subject of boarding order entirely. Instead there's a second argument sitting right behind the first one, waiting for its own instrument.
